ownerThemes.theme: Owners who compared it with the TL-2010Q say there is not much difference other than price; the micro lift does not raise the foot much but is handy on very thick seams.
A retailer explainer frames the differences as more included feet and the micro lifter on the TL-18QVP, with the same 8.5 in throat and 1,500 spm on both machines.

The other 1,500 spm straight stitch quilter in the class, usually several hundred dollars less

A computerized 10 in throat machine at a similar price for quilters who also want utility stitches

editorial.verdict: The TL-18QVP is the TL-2010Q with a micro lifter, more feet and dealer only distribution. The 8.5 in throat and 1,500 spm are identical, so the decision is whether the Float function and dealer support are worth the premium.
editorial.whoFor: A quilter or bag maker who wants a fast, simple straight stitch machine, sews bulky seams often, and prefers buying from a local Juki dealer.
editorial.skipIf: You need any stitch other than straight, you want the lowest price on this platform (TL-2010Q), or you want to quilt on a frame with regulated stitches (that is a different class of machine).

weaknesses: Straight stitch only; no zigzag, no buttonhole
8.5 in throat is domestic class despite "18" in the model name
Dealer only pricing varies; the published Juki page says contact a dealer

checks.title: Do not read the model number as arm length
checks.body: TL-18QVP has an 8.5 in throat. The 18 is a model designation, not inches.

checks.title: Compare the feet list against the TL-2010Q
checks.body: The extra feet are a real part of the price difference. Check which feet you would buy anyway.

checks.title: Ask the dealer about frame mounting
checks.body: Juki QVP sells frames for this class, but the machine has no stitch regulator. On a frame you control stitch length by hand speed.
